classification.difficultyReason: Use equal and parallel sides to identify intermediate lengths, then apply Pythagoras repeatedly.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals in these diagrams.

spec.description: Right triangle with base 24, right vertical side x and hypotenuse 30.
Triangle with equal base halves, total base 48, right side 25 and perpendicular height x.

answer.worked:
Each half of the base is $48\div2=24$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+24^2&=25^2\\x^2&=625-576\\x^2&=49\\x&=7\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Diamond with perpendicular diagonals, horizontal halves 8 and 8, equal vertical halves y, and outer labels 10, x and z.
Parallel bases 22 and 12, equal outer top segments, side 13 and two perpendiculars, the left labelled x.
spec.mathematics: Each outer top segment is (22−12)/2=5; x²+5²=13².

answer.worked:
The perpendiculars enclose a rectangle of width $12$. Each outer top segment is $(22-12)\div2=5$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+5^2&=13^2\\x^2&=169-25\\x^2&=144\\x&=12\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallelogram with both parallel-pair marks; side 21, side 20, top-right segment 16 and highlighted dashed diagonal x and altitude.
spec.answerVisibility: The highlighted construction is a permanent supplied given; its lengths remain unknown.

answer.worked:
Let the perpendicular height be $h$.
$$\begin{align*}h^2+16^2&=20^2\\h^2&=400-256\\h^2&=144\\h&=12\end{align*}$$
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, so the remaining top segment is $21-16=5$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=12^2+5^2\\x^2&=169\\x&=13\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Rectangle with width 9 and height 32, extended base 15 and a straight sloping line split into unknown x outside and 15 inside.
spec.mathematics: Internal vertical drop=√(15²−9²)=12; exterior height=32−12=20; x²=15²+20².
spec.answerVisibility: Both distinct source measurements 15 are retained.

answer.worked:
Let the vertical drop along the inside triangle be $h$.
$$\begin{align*}h^2+9^2&=15^2\\h^2&=225-81\\h^2&=144\\h&=12\end{align*}$$
The outside triangle has vertical side $32-12=20$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=15^2+20^2\\x^2&=625\\x&=25\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Source schematic of three connected right triangles along a shared baseline; retain right-angle indications and lengths 4, 3, 12 and 85 without treating the sketch as to scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Only x, y and z identify the requested lengths.

answer.short:
$x=5,\ y=13,\ z=84$

Apply Pythagoras successively to the three marked right triangles.

spec.description: Outer rectangle of width 28 surrounding an inner quadrilateral with four marked right angles and two adjacent sides 20. Both source occurrences of x, and labels 16, y, z and w, are retained.
spec.mathematics: x²+16²=20²; outer height=x+16; inner quadrilateral is a square, enabling successive right-triangle calculations.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated side lengths are printed.

answer.short:
$x=12,\ y=16,\ z=12,\ w=16$

The inner figure is a square; use Pythagoras in the corner triangles.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+16^2&=20^2\\x^2&=400-256\\x^2&=144\\x&=12\\w&=28-12\\w&=16\end{align*}$$
The inner quadrilateral has four right angles and adjacent sides of length $20$, so it is a square. Its lower-right side is therefore $20$.
$$\begin{align*}z^2+16^2&=20^2\\z^2&=144\\z&=12\end{align*}$$
The outer rectangle has height $12+16=28$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=28-12\\y&=16\end{align*}$$

teachingContext.methodNote: Page 3 states Pythagoras and demonstrates substitution, evaluation and taking the positive square root. Page 5 applies it to a rectangle diagonal. Page 7 Example 4 and page 8 Example 5 retain the unknown squared term, subtract the known square and take the square root to find a shorter side. Page 9 concerns the converse and contains printed errors; those erroneous comparisons are not used.
teachingContext.mappingNote: Part a directly finds a shorter side. Part b first halves an equally divided base. Part c uses perpendicular equal half-diagonals. Part d uses parallel bases and equal overhangs. Part e finds a height and then a diagonal. Part f finds the internal vertical drop before the outside hypotenuse. Part g applies the theorem successively to three marked triangles. Part h combines the corner triangles with equal opposite rectangle sides and the inner square. These directly assess multistep side-finding rather than area or converse testing.
